item.title: [xinference] Xinference vulnerable to remote code execution via unsafe `eval()` in Llama3 tool-call parsing | Security Advisory for Python packages hosted at PyPI.org
item.description: SummaryXinference used Python's unsafe eval() function when parsing Llama3 tool-call output generated by a large language model. Because the model output can be influenced by attacker-controlled promp
item.content:encoded: SummaryXinference used Python's unsafe eval() function when parsing Llama3 tool-call output generated by a large language model. Because the model output can be influenced by attacker-controlled prompts sent to the chat completion API, a remote attacker can craft prompts that cause the model to return a Python expression. Xinference then evaluates that expression on the server while post-processing the tool-call result. In the tested default deployment, authentication was not enabled, so the vul

enclosure.alt: Xinference vulnerable to remote code execution via unsafe `eval()` in Llama3 tool-call parsing

item.title: [gettext-converter] gettext-converter: Prototype pollution in js2i18next() via crafted translation keys | Security Advisory for JavaScript packages hosted at npmjs.com
item.description: Impactjs2i18next() is vulnerable to prototype pollution. When converting translations, it splits nested keys on the key separator (default ##) and uses each segment as a dynamic object key while build
item.content:encoded: Impactjs2i18next() is vulnerable to prototype pollution. When converting translations, it splits nested keys on the key separator (default ##) and uses each segment as a dynamic object key while building the output object. A key whose segment is __proto__ (e.g. __proto__##gcPolluted) causes the converter to resolve Object.prototype as the nested write target and assign the translated value onto it, polluting Object.prototype for the whole runtime.Any application that converts translation data (P

enclosure.alt: gettext-converter: Prototype pollution in js2i18next() via crafted translation keys

item.content:encoded: ImpactThe HTTP route handler exported by next-video/request-handler — which the README instructs consumers to mount at /api/video — allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to read arbitrary .json files from the production filesystem of any application following the documented setup.The handler's GET endpoint accepts a url query parameter and uses it to locate and serve a JSON asset descriptor from disk.
